Indoor Gardening

The Prettiest Indoor Gardens

Pretty Indoor Gardens

If you’ve ever wanted to grow your own herbs, greens, or microgreens indoors…

but cringed at the idea of clunky plastic gadgets taking over your kitchen counter, you’re not alone.

Most hydroponic systems work well…

But let’s be honest, many of them look like science experiments.

The good news?

You don’t have to choose between style and sustainability.

There are now countertop hydroponic systems that are both functional and beautiful.

Whether you’re into clean minimalism, Japandi neutrals, or a soft modern vibe, here are my favorite indoor gardens that keep things green without throwing off your whole aesthetic.

What Makes an Aesthetic Indoor Garden

I grow everything inside my apartment since I don’t have any outdoor space.

And because I live in a small, NYC apartment, aesthetics matter.

I always get people commenting, “You can DIY a hydroponic setup and it’ll be way cheaper!”

But to me, that misses the point.

I don’t just want to grow fresh herbs and vegetables… I also want my space to feel calm, intentional, and beautiful.

I’m not looking to turn my apartment into a hodge-podge science lab in the process!

My favorite systems blend into my home and combine function with thoughtful design.

Here’s what I look for when recommending a stylish indoor garden setup:

  • Neutral tones: White, soft grey, matte black, or natural wood
  • Compact shape: Something that doesn’t take up too much space
  • Materials that feel elevated: ceramic, glass, or matte metal
  • Concealed cords and water tanks: I hate wires and cords all over the place
  • Soft grow lights: Not harsh blue or purple lighting that makes your space feel like an office building

When I first started growing vegetables inside my apartment years ago, there was really just one company offering all-in-one hydroponic gardens.

Today, there are so many options!

So thankfully, whether you want to grow basil or broccoli sprouts, form and function can absolutely coexist.

just a couple of the indoor gardens I’ve tried!

Farel Sprouting Kit

Minimalist | No electricity | Stackable + compact

If you’ve never been able to keep a plant alive, this is your new best friend.

The Farel Sprouting Kit is hands down the easiest way to grow something edible indoors: no lights, no electricity, and no green thumb required.

It comes with stackable glass jars and stainless steel mesh lids that let you rinse and drain your seeds effortlessly.

Wit the Farel Kit, you don’t need soil or a grow light.

Just soak your seeds, rinse them twice a day, and in about 3–5 days you’ll have a fresh batch of sprouts ready to eat.

Sprouts and microgreens are some of the most nutrient-dense foods you can grow at home.

They’ve been shown to contain significantly higher concentrations of vitamins, antioxidants, and enzymes compared to their mature counterparts.

For example, broccoli sprouts can contain up to 40x more sulforaphane (a powerful compound linked to detoxification, reduced inflammation, and cancer prevention) than full-grown broccoli.

Plus, since you’re harvesting them just days after germination, the nutrients haven’t had time to degrade like they do with grocery store produce that’s been sitting in transport and on shelves.

If you’re new to indoor gardening, the Farel Kit is the ultimate low-commitment way to start!

It takes up barely any space, it looks great on a shelf or counter, and it adds a major health upgrade to your meals.

Sprinkle sprouts onto salads, sandwiches, avocado toast, or even blend them into smoothies!

Ingarden Microgreens Garden

Design-forward | Ceramic + metal | Microgreens made easy

If you love the idea of growing microgreens but want something with a little more structure and a lot more style, the Ingarden Microgreens Garden is the next step up.

With its ceramic base, stainless steel tray, and built-in LED light, this is the microgreens setup that doubles as functional kitchen decor.

Unlike simple sprouting jars, the Ingarden is a fully automated hydroponic system built specifically for growing microgreens.

It waters your seeds on a schedule, provides soft overhead lighting, and supports denser, more robust growth than passive kits.

So if you’re looking for lush, picture-perfect trays of greens that grow evenly, reliably and quickly, this is it.

But it’s not just about looks.

Microgreens grown in the Ingarden are packed with nutrients, including vitamins A, C, E, and K, as well as minerals like iron and potassium.

Studies have shown they can contain 5–40x more nutrients than their mature vegetable counterparts.

And because the Ingarden system is hands-off and super consistent, it delivers results week after week without the trial and error of manual rinsing or drainage.

So choose this over a simple sprouting kit like Farel if:

  • you want something that can be left alone (no rinsing required)
  • you prefer a sleeker, more refined design
  • you want to grow denser trays of greens (vs. smaller, simpler sprouts)
  • you’re interested in a gift-worthy setup that’s both functional and beautiful

The Ingarden is ideal if you want to consistently grow multiple microgreens on an automated schedule, without fuss.

And I love how it looks like it belongs on a Pinterest board!

If you love topping your meals with spicy radish or colorful purple kohlrabi sprouts, this is a beautiful way to do it!

How to Style Your Indoor Garden

Hydroponic systems can look just as polished as your favorite cookbooks or ceramic jars if you give them a little styling love.

Here’s suggestions to make them feel more integrated with the rest of your home decor:

  • Set it on a wooden tray or marble slab to visually anchor the space
  • Tuck it beside a lamp or under-cabinet light for soft ambient glow
  • Use matching accessories like a ceramic watering can or neutral microfiber cloth for cleaning
  • Hide or manage cords with cord covers or cable organizers
  • Surround it with natural textures like linen towels, wood boards, or matte jars to tie everything together

Keep Things Clean + Aesthetic

  • Wipe down the exterior once a week to avoid dust or mineral spots
  • Trim plants regularly to keep their shape tidy and encourage more growth
  • Prevent herbs and lettuces bolt or flower (snip those buds to keep growth compact!)
  • Avoid growing fruiting plants if you don’t want to vacuum fallen buds

FAQs About Aesthetic Hydroponic Systems

Can I turn off the grow lights at night?

Most systems have built-in timers. The lights cycle on and off automatically, usually 16 hours on, 8 hours off.

Do these make noise?

The gardens I’ve recommended above are all silent, without a water pump so there’s no noise whatsoever.

Can I grow flowers?

Yes! Edible flowers like nasturtiums or violas can work in hydroponic systems. Just make sure you pick varieties that stay compact.

What if I want to grow multiple things at once?

The Counterstand and Smart Garden 9 (the larger version of the Click and Grow) are great for this.

You can grow a full mix of herbs, lettuce, and edible flowers without sacrificing style.
